questions.prompt: What is the primary function of video captions?

options.text: To provide a spoken narration of visual elements.
To change the color palette of the video automatically.
To provide a text version of the spoken words and essential sounds.
To increase the loading speed of the video player.

questions.explanation: Captions convert the audio track of a video into readable text for users who cannot hear it.
questions.hint: Consider how spoken dialogue is represented on screen.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand the difference between captions and audio descriptions.

questions.prompt: Why is it risky to rely entirely on unedited automatic captions?

options.text: They usually display in a font size that is too large.
They often contain confusing or incorrect information and require human review.
They are forbidden by accessibility guidelines.
They drain the battery life of mobile devices too quickly.

questions.explanation: Automatic captions frequently make mistakes, which can completely change the meaning of the spoken words without a manual review.
questions.hint: Think about how well computer software understands different accents or complex words.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize why automatic captions require human review.

options.text: People with low vision or blindness who need a spoken narration of on-screen visual elements.
People who are watching a video in a loud, crowded room.
Designers who are checking the contrast ratio of the video player.
Developers who want to decrease the video file size.

questions.explanation: Audio descriptions provide critical context for visual actions that cannot be understood through the standard audio track alone.
questions.hint: Consider what happens when a video shows an important action but nobody speaks.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify who benefits from accessible multimedia.
